description: Feature backlog - Product Owner owns priority

items.title: Sprint summary report as markdown artifact
items.intent: After a batch run completes, aishore must produce a shareable markdown sprint report showing every item shipped, pass/fail status, duration, lines changed, regression suite results, core health, and totals — so users have a viral proof artifact they can paste in Slack or commit to the repo.
items.description: The sprint report is the single highest-ROI feature for adoption. When run done or run N completes, drop a markdown file (e.g. .aishore/data/reports/sprint-YYYY-MM-DD.md) and print a summary to stdout. Include: item table (ID, title, status, duration, lines +/-), regression suite stats, core health, heal items generated, and totals. Format it to be impressive when pasted in Slack or viewed on GitHub.
steps: Create a report generation function that reads sprint archive data for the current batch
Build the markdown template with item table, regression stats, core health, and totals
Call the report generator at end of batch run (after all items processed)
Write report to .aishore/data/reports/ with date-stamped filename
Print a compact version to stdout as the batch completion message

acceptanceCriteria.text: Report generation function exists in codebase
Report contains item table with ID, title, status, duration, lines changed
Compact summary printed to stdout at batch end

items.groomingNotes: Must-priority. Steps now specify exact function name (_generate_sprint_report), data sources (sprint_items[], COMPLETED_IDS, FAILED_IDS, batch_start — all already in scope in cmd_run), and output format. Reports go to .aishore/data/reports/ (directory does not yet exist — developer must create it). AC verify #1 combines run done + file existence check; verify #2 and #3 are real assertions (fallbacks removed). Verify #4 checks that the report path appears in run output. Developer must run run done after implementing to generate the first report before AC can pass.

items.title: Composable quality gates via config
items.intent: Teams must be able to declare custom quality gate commands in config.yaml (pre-flight, post-develop, pre-merge phases) that run alongside built-in gates — so aishore adds intent gates and regression protection on top of existing CI checks rather than replacing them, making adoption additive.
items.description: Add a gates section to config.yaml where users can add custom shell commands at each pipeline phase: pre_flight (before dev starts), post_develop (after dev, before validation), pre_merge (after validation, before merge). Each gate has a name and command. Built-in gates (regression suite, maturity protocol, validator agent) remain; custom gates run alongside them. A failing custom gate blocks the pipeline just like a built-in gate.
steps: Define gates schema in config.yaml with pre_flight, post_develop, pre_merge phases
Parse gate definitions from config during sprint setup
Execute custom gates at each phase alongside built-in gates
Report gate results (name, pass/fail, output) in sprint log
Include custom gate results in sprint report

acceptanceCriteria.text: Custom gates can be defined in config.yaml under a gates section
A failing custom gate blocks the sprint pipeline
Gate results appear in sprint logs

items.groomingNotes: Steps now specify exact hook points: _run_preflight (after regression suite), post-developer-pass (before validation), post-validator-pass (before merge). Gate runner takes phase name and returns 1 on failure. Requires yq for config parsing — graceful no-op when yq absent or gates section missing. Not marking ready: needs scoping decision on whether yq is required (currently optional). AC verify #3 is true-deferred — integration test needs a real sprint run with a custom gate. Developer should manually test with a gates.pre_flight: [{name: smoke, command: false}] to confirm blocking behavior before signaling pass.

items.title: GitHub Action for CI/headless sprint execution
items.intent: Users must be able to run aishore in GitHub Actions on a schedule or trigger so that pushing a PRODUCT.md change or adding a backlog item causes sprints to execute in CI and open PRs automatically — enabling the overnight factory workflow where you wake up to shipped features.
items.description: Create a GitHub Action (action.yml + wrapper script) that runs aishore run in a CI environment. Needs: Claude API key as secret, gh token for PR creation, headless mode (no interactive prompts). Pairs with --pr mode (FEAT-121) so CI runs produce PRs rather than auto-merging to main. Include a sample workflow yaml users can copy.
steps: Create action.yml defining the GitHub Action inputs (api key, run args, pr mode)
Create entrypoint script that sets up environment and runs aishore
Handle headless Claude Code execution (CLAUDE_CODE_HEADLESS or equivalent)
Create sample workflow file (.github/workflows/aishore.yml) users can copy
Document CI setup in README or dedicated CI doc

acceptanceCriteria.text: action.yml exists and defines required inputs
Entrypoint handles missing interactive terminal gracefully

items.title: Agent-agnostic backend abstraction for developer and validator agents
items.intent: The orchestration layer must support pluggable AI backends (not just Claude Code) via a config-driven agent backend setting — so that users of Aider, Codex CLI, or other tools can adopt aishore for its quality model (intent gates, regression protection, core-first discipline) without switching their AI tool.
items.description: Abstract the agent invocation layer so the developer and validator agents can be backed by different tools. Start with claude-code as the default backend. Define a backend interface: a command template that receives the prompt file and working directory, returns exit code and result.json. Add backend config to config.yaml. This is a design-now, ship-incrementally feature — the abstraction should be clean even if only claude-code is implemented initially.
steps: Define agent backend interface: input (prompt file, workdir, context), output (exit code, result.json)
Extract current Claude Code invocation into a backend module
Add agent.backend config to config.yaml with claude-code as default
Create backend dispatch function that routes to the configured backend
Document how to add a custom backend

acceptanceCriteria.text: Agent invocation goes through a backend abstraction layer
claude-code backend works identically to current behavior

items.groomingNotes: Could priority refactor. Steps specify extracting existing claude invocation into _invoke_agent() dispatch function — this is a refactor, not a new feature. Risk: touching the agent invocation path could break the sprint loop. Not marking ready: this is a significant refactor that should not block feature delivery. Recommend tackling after FEAT-120 and FEAT-121 ship. Developer should read the existing claude invocation in .aishore/aishore before implementing to identify all call sites.

items.title: Chicken-and-egg: regression fix items cannot run because regressions block pre-flight
items.intent: When a backlog item exists specifically to fix the regression suite (like BUG-154), the orchestrator must allow it to bypass the pre-flight regression check — because requiring the regression suite to pass before running the item that fixes the regression suite creates an unresolvable deadlock that requires manual intervention.
items.description: BUG-154 was created to fix stale regression entries blocking pre-flight. But BUG-154 itself could not run because pre-flight (which runs the regression suite) failed. This is a fundamental design flaw: the system cannot self-heal regression suite issues. Options: (1) items tagged track:core or with specific keywords bypass pre-flight, (2) if an items intent/title references regression suite, skip regression pre-flight for that item, (3) add a --skip-preflight flag for manual override, (4) if pre-flight fails, auto-check if any queued item is specifically about fixing regressions.
steps: In the sprint item picker or preflight runner, check if the picked item has a scope or title that indicates it fixes the regression suite
If the item is tagged track:core and its title/intent mentions regression, skip the regression preflight for that item only
Log a warning when skipping preflight so the user knows it was intentionally bypassed
Add a --skip-preflight flag to run command as a manual escape hatch

acceptanceCriteria.text: Items fixing regressions can bypass preflight

items.groomingNotes: Chicken-and-egg deadlock: regression fix items cannot pass the regression suite they are fixing. Solution: detect regression-fix items and skip preflight, plus manual --skip-preflight flag.

items.title: backlog check --all is too slow for use in regression suite
items.intent: backlog check --all must complete within 10 seconds for a typical backlog (20 items) — because the current implementation runs every verify command for every item sequentially, taking over 30 seconds for 16 items, which makes it unusable as a regression check and causes timeouts.
items.description: backlog check --all runs check_readiness_gates for each non-done item, which executes all AC verify commands. With 16 items, some having verify commands that themselves invoke aishore CLI commands, this takes over 30 seconds. The regression check for FEAT-103 was removed because it reliably timed out. Options: (1) parallelize verify command execution, (2) add --quick flag that skips verify commands, (3) cache recent verify results.
steps: In _backlog_check_all in cmd-backlog-read.sh, add a --quick flag that skips verify command execution and only checks metadata gates (intent, AC existence, dependencies)
Make the default behavior remain unchanged (full check with verify commands)
The quick check should complete in under 2 seconds for 20 items

acceptanceCriteria.text: backlog check --all --quick runs without executing verify commands

items.groomingNotes: Low priority quality-of-life improvement. Quick mode skips verify execution, checks only metadata readiness gates.
